facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. is a highly leveraged, now almost entirely U.S. out-of-home advertiser whose reported earnings are improving while its debt stack is unchanged. On the issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA of 544.3 for the twelve months to June 30, 2026 (FY2025 of 504.8 plus H1 2026 of 247.3 less H1 2025 of 207.8), debt principal including finance leases of 5,148.8 is 9.46x and, net of 192.1 of continuing cash, 9.11x, down from 10.20x and 9.82x at FY2025. Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest paid of 390.1 only 1.40x, against 1.28x for FY2025 and 1.09x for FY2024. Revenue for the twelve months is 1,679.1 against 1,604.1 for FY2025, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin is 32.4%. Free cash flow, defined here as operating cash flow of 160.4 less capital expenditures of 76.1, is 84.3; both inputs include discontinued operations. Debt principal barely changed between December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026: every note and term-loan balance is identical, and only finance leases moved, down 0.1. So the leverage improvement is earnings-led. The structure is 3,340.0 of first-priority secured debt (a 425.0 term loan and 2,915.0 of senior secured notes), 1,805.3 of senior unsecured notes due 2028 and 2029, and undrawn facilities; the secured share of principal is high, and the unsecured notes are effectively subordinated to it. Liquidity is 192.1 of cash and 205.5 of excess availability under a 100.0 revolving facility and a 200.0 receivables-based facility, both maturing June 12, 2030. The next significant maturities are in 2028, when 899.3 of 7.750% senior notes and the 425.0 term loan fall due, and the company has issued conditional redemption notices for the 2028 and 2029 unsecured notes, with conditions that include the merger closing. Operating lease liabilities of 1,361.9 and 877.6 of non-lease non-cancelable contracts at December 31, 2025 sit outside debt. Three qualifications bound this view. First, Adjusted EBITDA is the issuer's non-GAAP measure and is stated after site lease expense; the covenant EBITDA is not supplied. Second, cash-flow figures include the Spain business that was held for sale and the 2025 cash flows of businesses sold in 2025. Third, nothing after August 5, 2026 is supplied, so the merger, the redemption notices and the use of Spain sale proceeds, which are described as pending, cannot be reflected.

facts.label: Definition and basis risks
facts.text: 1. Adjusted EBITDA is the issuer's non-GAAP measure: loss from continuing operations plus tax, non-operating items, other operating expense, depreciation and amortization, share-based compensation, and restructuring and other costs (S7 page:7). It is after site lease expense, which sits in direct operating expenses (S4 page:24) and includes minimum guaranteed payments and revenue-sharing rent (S4 page:13). Covenant EBITDA is not supplied. 2. Total debt used here is principal including finance leases before discount and fees. The issuer's printed total and net debt are on carrying value (S7 page:6); the difference at June 30, 2026 is 41.1 (C3). 3. The FY2024 debt includes the CCIBV term loan, which belonged to businesses later sold; FY2024 leverage is shown with a sensitivity excluding it (C3). 4. Cash flow figures include discontinued operations (S4 page:7, page:8), while Adjusted EBITDA is continuing operations only. Trailing operating cash flow and capital expenditures include Spain in all periods and businesses sold in 2025 in FY2025 and H1 2025. 5. The Q3 2025 Adjusted EBITDA is derived from three printed figures and not printed in the supplied set. 6. The revenue mix between contracts with customers and leases changed sharply year over year because of changed contract terms (S4 page:15); that does not change total revenue. 7. Net income and cash flow for H1 2025 include large one-time items from the 2025 disposals (S4 page:11), so the trailing figures rely on continuing operations. 8. All balances are at June 30, 2026, before the Spain sale and the pending merger-related actions.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. is a listed U.S. out-of-home advertising operator with no controlling holder identified in the supplied sources, whose creditor story is a simplified, almost entirely domestic business sitting under a heavy, mostly unchanged debt stack while a take-private merger is pending. The operating base is roadside billboards and street furniture in the America segment and airport concessions in the Airports segment, together more than 64,500 displays at June 30, 2026, with digital displays a small share of inventory but a large share of revenue. Revenue is sold in short periods, mostly four weeks in roadside, against site leases and municipal and airport concessions that run for years with minimum guaranteed payments, so revenue visibility is short while the main cost is fixed or semi-fixed. That asymmetry is sharper in Airports, where site lease expense was 59.2% of revenue in H1 2026 against 31.3% in America (C1), so airport growth carries more fixed rent. Seasonality is steady: first quarter weakest and fourth quarter strongest. The credit-relevant history is a multi-year exit from international markets, completed with the sale of Spain on August 4, 2026, and a sequence of refinancings that moved secured maturities out to 2031 and 2033 while leaving the unsecured notes in 2028 and 2029. The transaction that matters most is the merger signed on February 9, 2026 with Madison Parent Inc., at 2.43 per share in cash, approved by stockholders on May 12, 2026 and expected, per the latest filing, to close by the end of the third quarter of 2026. The merger agreement lets either party terminate if closing has not happened by November 9, 2026, extendable to February 9, 2027 if regulatory approvals are outstanding, so the cutoff of November 5, 2026 falls four days before the first outside date, and the supplied sources do not say whether closing occurred. Debt amendments and conditional redemption notices tied to the merger exist, but they are described as pending. Ownership of the equity after closing, the merger financing, and the executed debt documents are not supplied. Documented issuer actions so far are mostly supportive or neutral for creditors, with disposal proceeds applied to debt and no dividends; none of the creditor-adverse actions in the method's checklist is documented in the supplied filings, which is a statement about the sources, not a finding about the executed documents.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The pending transaction is the take-private merger. On February 9, 2026 the company agreed to be acquired by an investor consortium of affiliates and/or certain investment funds advised by Mubadala Capital through Madison Parent Inc. and Madison Merger Sub Inc., with Merger Sub merging into the company, which would survive as a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent (S1 page:4; S4 page:8). Holders of common stock would receive 2.43 per share in cash. The Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period expired on April 9, 2026 and stockholders approved the agreement on May 12, 2026 (S4 page:8). The latest filing says closing is expected by the end of the third quarter of 2026, subject to remaining customary conditions including review by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (S4 page:8). The annual report adds termination rights if the merger is not consummated on or before November 9, 2026, extendable to February 9, 2027 if requisite regulatory approvals are not obtained, a termination fee payable by the company of 39.8 million, or 19.9 million during the go-shop period, and a fee payable by Parent of 92.9 million under certain other circumstances (S1 page:24; S1 page:53; S1 page:54). The company has represented that the buyer has sufficient funds, but it also warns that the equity and debt financing contemplated by the merger agreement must be funded or closed (S1 page:24). The financing amounts, the sources of the buyer's equity and the post-closing capital structure are Not supplied. Until closing, the agreement restricts the company from incurring certain debt, paying dividends, settling certain proceedings and incurring certain capital expenditures without the buyer's written consent (S1 page:25). The first outside date, November 9, 2026, falls four days after the cutoff of November 5, 2026, and nothing in the supplied sources reports whether the merger closed or the dates moved.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The merger has direct debt consequences, all described as pending at August 5, 2026. In April 2026 the company completed consent solicitations with holders of its senior secured notes and with the lenders under its credit agreement, and in May 2026 with the lenders under its receivables-based credit agreement, entering into supplemental indentures and amendments dated April 9, April 10 and May 15, 2026 (S4 page:8; S4 page:9; S4 page:38; S4 page:39). These provide that the merger will not constitute a change of control under the debt documents; the supplemental indentures and the credit agreement amendment are effective but become operative only on consummation of the merger, and cease to be effective if it is not completed (S4 page:16). The receivables-based amendment, when effective, would extend the maturity of that facility to five years from the merger, raise revolving commitments from 200.0 million to 250.0 million, broaden the borrowing base and permit qualified securitisation financings (S4 page:16; S4 page:17). The company has also issued conditional notices of redemption for the 7.750% Senior Notes due 2028 and the 7.500% Senior Notes due 2029, conditional on closing (S4 page:17). Together these actions would remove the 2028 and 2029 unsecured maturities and keep the secured notes outstanding with changed change-of-control terms, but the consent terms, the redemption price and the source of redemption funds are Not supplied, and the executed supplemental indentures and amendments are cited in the exhibit list but not supplied (S4 page:38; S4 page:39). No new debt was issued in the first half of 2026: the six-month cash flow shows 145 thousand of debt repayments and no issuance line (S4 page:5).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Earlier new debt issues explain the current stack. In March 2024 the company issued 865.0 million of 7.875% Senior Secured Notes due 2030 and used part of the proceeds to prepay 835.0 million of its term loan, refinancing the remaining 425.0 million and extending its maturity to August 2028 (S1 page:69; S1 page:107). On August 4, 2025 it issued 1,150.0 million of 7.125% Senior Secured Notes due 2031 and 900.0 million of 7.500% Senior Secured Notes due 2033, and with cash on hand redeemed 1,250.0 million of 5.125% and 750.0 million of 9.000% senior secured notes; it paid 62.0 million of accrued interest, a 36.1 million redemption premium and 26.3 million of other fees, and recognised a 43.8 million loss on extinguishment (S1 page:69; S1 page:102). In June 2025 it extended the revolving and receivables-based facilities to June 12, 2030, reduced the revolver from 115.8 million to 100.0 million and raised the receivables-based facility from 175.0 million to 200.0 million (S1 page:102). In the second quarter of 2025 it repurchased 95.7 million of 7.750% and 134.1 million of 7.500% senior notes in the open market for 203.4 million including accrued interest and fees, recognising a gain of 28.8 million; the repurchased notes are held by the company and not cancelled (S1 page:102). The debt register, maturities and liquidity are in the CP-1 handoff: principal is 5,148.8 million at June 30, 2026 and no significant maturities fall before 2028.

On August 4, 2025 it issued 1,150.0 million of 7.125% Senior Secured Notes due 2031 and 900.0 million of 7.500% Senior Secured Notes due 2033, and with cash on hand redeemed 1,250.0 million of 5.125% and 750.0 million of 9.000% senior secured notes; it paid 62.0 million of accrued interest, a 36.1 million redemption premium and 26.3 million of other fees, and recognised a 43.8 million loss on extinguishment (S1 page:69; S1 page:102). In June 2025 it extended the revolving and receivables-based facilities to June 12, 2030, reduced the revolver from 115.8 million to 100.0 million and raised the receivables-based facility from 175.0 million to 200.0 million (S1 page:102). In the second quarter of 2025 it repurchased 95.7 million of 7.750% and 134.1 million of 7.500% senior notes in the open market for 203.4 million including accrued interest and fees, recognising a gain of 28.8 million; the repurchased notes are held by the company and not cancelled (S1 page:102). The debt register, maturities and liquidity are in the CP-1 handoff: principal is 5,148.8 million at June 30, 2026 and no significant maturities fall before 2028.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The disposal programme is the other transaction thread. The company sold Switzerland, Italy and France in 2023, Mexico, Peru and Chile on February 5, 2025 for 34.0 million, the Europe-North segment to Bauer Radio Limited on March 31, 2025 for 625.0 million (net cash proceeds 572.0 million, part used to prepay the 375.0 million CCIBV term loan), and Brazil on October 1, 2025 for 15.0 million (S1 page:93; S1 page:94). It used proceeds and cash on hand to reduce indebtedness by approximately 605 million in 2025 (S1 page:55). The Spain sale agreed on September 7, 2025 for approximately 115 million euros (S2 page:9; S1 page:94) completed on August 4, 2026 for a purchase price of approximately 132.3 million dollars, with net proceeds subject to adjustments and fees; the company intends to use them to reduce debt, subject to the outcome of the merger (S4 page:9; S4 page:22). That completion is a subsequent event to the June 30, 2026 balance sheet and is not in the balance-sheet figures. At the offer price, equity consideration on 509,093,845 basic shares outstanding at July 31, 2026 is about 1,237.1 million before equity awards and any other dilutive instruments (C2); the supplied sources do not state the fully diluted equity value or the enterprise value.

rows.label: Clear Channel Outdoor is a U.S. roadside and airport advertiser with long-dated site contracts and heavy fixed rent. A take-private merger at 2.43 per share is pending, and its status after August 5, 2026 is unknown.
The merger agreement allows termination if the merger has not closed by November 9, 2026, extendable to February 9, 2027 if regulatory approvals are outstanding.
Amendments to the secured notes and credit agreement make the merger not a change of control, but they become operative only on closing.
Airports Segment Adjusted EBITDA margin was 25.3% in H1 2026 against 41.0% for America, because airport site lease expense was 59.2% of revenue.
Substantially all international operations were sold in 2025 and 2026, and sale proceeds and cash reduced indebtedness by about 605 million in 2025.
Beneficial ownership is not in the supplied sources because the annual report defers it to an amendment that is not supplied.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage has eased, but only through earnings. Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. carries debt principal of USD 5,148.8 million at June 30, 2026 against USD 5,148.9 million at December 31, 2025, while trailing Adjusted EBITDA is USD 544.3 million against USD 504.8 million for FY2025. Total debt to Adjusted EBITDA is therefore 9.46x, down from 10.20x, and 9.11x net of USD 192.1 million of cash. Because principal has not moved, leverage will rise as quickly as it fell if earnings decline: a 10% fall in trailing Adjusted EBITDA would put the ratio at about 10.51x (Documentary Fact for the inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the sensitivity). The measure is the issuer's own non-GAAP figure, stated after site lease expense, and the covenant definition is not supplied.

First-priority secured debt is USD 3,340.0 million, or 6.14x trailing Adjusted EBITDA and about 64.9% of principal, made up of a USD 425.0 million term loan and USD 2,915.0 million of senior secured notes due 2030, 2031 and 2033. The USD 1,805.3 million of senior unsecured notes due in 2028 and 2029 are effectively subordinated to that debt and structurally subordinated to non-guarantors, and the guarantor list is not supplied. The ratio is an indicator of secured leverage, not the covenant measure.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity is adequate for now, with the main maturities two years away. Cash is USD 192.1 million and excess availability under the revolver and receivables-based facility is USD 205.5 million, together USD 397.6 million, with no borrowings drawn and both facilities maturing June 12, 2030. That sum is about one year of the issuer's expected 2027 cash interest. Availability under the receivables-based facility depends on a borrowing base, and the revolver's springing first lien net leverage covenant of 7.10x was not in effect at June 30, 2026, so headroom cannot be measured. The next significant maturities are USD 1,324.6 million in 2028 (the 7.750% notes and the term loan) and USD 906.3 million in 2029, which together are about 43.3% of principal.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The pending merger dominates the capital structure outlook. The take-private merger at USD 2.43 per share was approved by stockholders on May 12, 2026 and was expected to close by the end of the third quarter of 2026, but its first outside date of November 9, 2026 falls four days after the cutoff and the supplied sources do not say whether it closed. Debt amendments make the merger not a change of control, but they become operative only on closing, and conditional redemption notices cover the 2028 and 2029 unsecured notes. The funding source and price of those redemptions and the buyer's financing are not supplied. Equity consideration on basic shares is about USD 1,237.1 million, about 24.0% of debt principal, so the offer implies a thin equity layer beneath the debt (Analyst Interpretation; no valuation or recovery view is stated).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Business risk is short-cycle revenue against fixed rent. Roadside advertising is mostly sold in four-week periods while site leases and municipal and airport concessions run for years, so a demand dip reaches margin before contracts roll. Airports Segment Adjusted EBITDA margin was 25.3% in H1 2026 against 41.0% for America because airport site lease expense was 59.2% of revenue, and airport minimum guarantees rise with prior-period performance. Revenue grew 8.7% in the second quarter of 2026 and Adjusted EBITDA grew 11.6%, partly on event-driven demand from the FIFA World Cup (Documentary Fact; the event effect is Analyst Interpretation as to repeatability).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Earnings momentum: trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 544.3 million is above the FY2025 level of USD 504.8 million, and H1 2026 Adjusted EBITDA grew about 19.0% over H1 2025 (Documentary Fact). Permit-protected, diversified inventory: more than 64,500 displays and operations in 81 U.S. markets at December 31, 2025, and no single advertiser is a material portion of revenue (Documentary Fact; the leading-position claims are Management Language and are not adopted). Liquidity and runway: USD 192.1 million of cash, USD 205.5 million of undrawn facilities maturing in June 2030, and no significant maturities before 2028 (Documentary Fact). Simplified, domestic business: substantially all international operations were sold, with the Spain sale completed on August 4, 2026, which simplifies the perimeter (Documentary Fact). No distributions: no dividends are intended and none are permitted while the merger agreement stands (Documentary Fact). Positive free cash flow: USD 84.3 million on the trailing basis against USD 32.0 million in FY2025 (Documentary Fact for inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the measure).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. High leverage with flat debt: 9.46x total debt and 9.11x net, with principal essentially unchanged, so deleveraging relies on earnings and asset sale proceeds (Analyst Interpretation from the financial base). Thin cover: cash interest cover of 1.40x and about 1.20x after capital expenditure leave limited room for an advertising downturn, and the stockholders' deficit is USD 3,457.1 million (Documentary Fact). Fixed airport rent: airport site lease expense at 59.2% of revenue makes the fastest-growing segment the lowest-margin one, and USD 1,361.9 million of operating lease liabilities sit outside the debt figure (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Refinancing concentration: about 43.3% of principal falls due in 2028 and 2029, and the unsecured notes rank behind USD 3,340.0 million of secured debt (Documentary Fact). Metro and sector concentration: America is about three quarters of revenue, Los Angeles is a leading market, and 2026 growth drew on technology advertisers in the San Francisco area (Documentary Fact). Unresolved ownership and merger outcome: control, merger financing, the post-closing capital plan and the consent terms are not supplied, and willingness of the prospective owner cannot be inferred from its identity (Insufficient Information). Information limits: covenant headroom, guarantor financials and executed documents are not supplied (Insufficient Information).

## Findings
### Reader summary

### Readiness view

### Information-availability boundary
- The latest supplied documents are dated August 5, 2026: the Q2 10-Q ("Date: August 5, 2026", page:39) and the Q2 release ("August 5, 2026", page:1).

- The window from August 6, 2026 to the cutoff of November 5, 2026 is not covered. Anything that happened in that window is Not supplied, not absent. This matters because the 10-Q states the merger "is expected to close by the end of the third quarter of 2026" (page:8), and the Spain sale closed on August 4, 2026, one day before the filing (page:9).
- No document for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 is supplied. The latest balance sheet date is June 30, 2026.
- Current period per context is q2-2026; the supplied set matches it. The prior period fy-2025 is matched by the 10-K.
### Source register
#### Form 10-K, fiscal year 2025 (10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl)

- Family and authority: filed annual report, original authority for audited consolidated statements. page:1 "FORM 10-K"; "FOR THE FISCAL YEAR ENDED DECEMBER 31, 2025"; Commission File Number 001-32663.

- Audit: page:75 auditor's report, signed Ernst & Young LLP, San Antonio, February 26, 2026 (page:77); one critical audit matter, goodwill valuation of the America and Airports reporting units (page:76).
- Statements: balance sheet page:77 and page:78; income statement page:78 (three years); cash flows page:79 and page:80; cash paid for interest and taxes page:80.

- Notes located: dispositions and discontinued operations page:93; segments page:98 to page:100; revenue page:100; long-term debt page:100 to page:117 (debt table page:100 and page:101, notes and facilities page:104 to page:116, maturities page:116 and page:117); leases page:117; commitments and contingencies page:118; asset retirement obligations page:125; subsequent events page:131.
- MD&A: liquidity and capital resources from page:62 (debt service and cash on hand page:66); credit-facility availability table page:68; debt covenants page:70.
- Units: thousands of USD in statements ("(In thousands, except per share data)", page:78); MD&A text in millions.

- Perimeter: Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. and subsidiaries, consolidated, including noncontrolling interests. Spain is a discontinued operation held for sale at year end; the former Europe-North segment and Latin American businesses (sold in 2025) are also in discontinued operations (page:4; Q2 10-Q page:7).

- Version relationship: the Part III items are "incorporated by reference from our Form 10-K/A" (page:135, page:136). That amendment is not supplied, so executive pay, ownership and related-party detail are Not supplied.

- Wording difference carried forward: the 10-K describes the buyer as an investor consortium of Mubadala Capital "in partnership with TWG Global" (page:4); the Q2 10-Q and Q2 release name Mubadala Capital funds without that phrase (Q2 10-Q page:8). This is a description difference, not a conflict of fact.
#### Form 10-Q, quarter ended September 30, 2025 (10-Q_2025-09-30_cco-20250930.htm.jsonl)

- Family and authority: filed unaudited interim report. Gives the third-quarter 2025 and nine-month 2025 and 2024 income statements (page:3), segment data (page:13), Spain sale agreement (page:9, "approximately €115 million"), the Brazil sale on October 1, 2025 (page:9, page:10), letters of credit and availability (page:20) and cash (page:40).

- Role: the only source for the third quarter 2025 three-month columns. The fourth quarter of 2025 is given in the February 2026 release (page:1), and the annual figure is in the 10-K, so a discrete third-quarter and fourth-quarter 2025 series can be located without a derived residual for revenue.

- Perimeter at that date: Brazil was still within discontinued operations as an asset held until its October 1, 2025 sale (page:10). It is superseded in time by the 10-K, which controls for December 31, 2025.
#### Form 10-Q, quarter ended March 31, 2026 (10-Q_2026-03-31_cco-20260331.htm.jsonl)

- Family and authority: filed unaudited interim report. First-quarter 2026 and 2025 income statement (page:3), discontinued operations (page:9), segments (page:11), letters of credit and the April 2026 consent solicitation as a subsequent event (page:15), credit-facility availability (page:30).
- Role: the only filed source for the first-quarter 2025 comparative columns on the current continuing-operations basis.
#### Form 10-Q, quarter ended June 30, 2026 (10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl)

- Family and authority: filed unaudited interim report, the latest and controlling source for June 30, 2026 balances and the three and six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025. Cover page:1; signature "Date: August 5, 2026" (page:39).

- Statements: balance sheet page:2 and page:3; income statement page:3; cash flows page:5 and page:6 (six months only; discontinued-operation cash flows are included and not separately presented, page:7 and page:8).

- Notes: basis of presentation and pending merger page:7 to page:9; dispositions and discontinued operations page:9 to page:11; segments page:12 to page:14; revenue page:14 and page:15; long-term debt and merger-related debt actions page:15 to page:17; commitments and contingencies page:17.
- MD&A: page:21 onward; liquidity page:29 to page:33; credit facilities table page:33 and page:34; debt covenants page:34.
- Units: thousands of USD in statements; credit-facility table in millions (page:33).

- Exhibit list page:38 and page:39 cites supplemental indentures dated April 9, 2026, a Seventh Amendment to Credit Agreement dated April 10, 2026 and a Third Amendment to Credit Agreement dated May 15, 2026. Those documents are incorporated by reference and are not supplied.
#### Earnings releases, Exhibit 99.1 (three files)

- Family and authority: issuer-prepared, unaudited, furnished releases. They give attributed management narrative and the issuer's non-GAAP measures: Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Corporate expenses, FFO and AFFO, with reconciliations (Q2 release page:8 to page:10; Q4 release page:9).

- The Q2 release adds an issuer-computed net debt line in its debt table (page:6, "Net debt $ 4,915,491 $ 4,912,971") and the Q1 release does the same (page:5). Net debt and the non-GAAP measures are issuer presentations, not filed GAAP statements. The statements inside the releases duplicate the matching 10-Q or 10-K and do not corroborate them independently. Where a release and a filing differ in wording or scope, the filing controls.
- Each release says the company "is not providing financial guidance" because of the merger (Q2 release page:1; Q4 release page:1), so no management outlook exists in the supplied set.
### Identity and perimeter

- Reporting entity: Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc., a Delaware corporation (10-K page:1). It is the issuer of every note and the borrower under the senior secured credit facilities; the receivables-based facility has the company and certain subsidiaries as borrowers (10-K page:104, page:107).

- Subsidiary guarantors: the notes and facilities are guaranteed by "certain" wholly owned domestic subsidiaries (10-K page:108, page:110). No guarantor list, no guarantor or non-guarantor financial information and no restricted or unrestricted subsidiary split is supplied. The context leaves borrower, parent and guarantor fields blank, which is not evidence that none exist.

- Pending owner: Madison Parent Inc., with Madison Merger Sub Inc. merging into the company, which would survive as a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent; the buyer is described as affiliates and funds advised by Mubadala Capital (Q2 10-Q page:8). Parent and Merger Sub are counterparties to the merger, not obligors on the existing debt as far as the supplied text shows.

- Operating perimeter on the current basis: two reportable segments, America and Airports, with Singapore in Other (Q2 10-Q page:12). Substantially all continuing revenue is from the U.S. (Q2 10-Q page:14). Spain is held for sale as of June 30, 2026 and sold on August 4, 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:9).

- Currency: USD throughout. No other reporting currency is used for continuing operations; the Spain price was set in euros (10-K page:73 and 10-Q Q3 2025 page:9) and is a discontinued-operation item.
### Period and basis map
| Period | Where located | Basis and caution |
| FY2025, FY2024, FY2023 | 10-K page:78 to page:80 | Audited, continuing operations, Spain in discontinued operations; segment data page:98 to page:100 |
| Q1 2025 and Q1 2026 | Q1 10-Q page:3, page:11; Q1 release | Unaudited; Q1 2025 appears only as a comparative column |
| Q2 2025 and Q2 2026, six months 2025 and 2026 | Q2 10-Q page:3, page:12, page:13; Q2 release page:1 | Unaudited; three-month and six-month columns must stay separate |
| Q3 2025, nine months 2025 | Q3 2025 10-Q page:3, page:13 | Unaudited; original presentation |
| Q4 2025 | Q4 release page:1, page:2 | Issuer release; the 10-K does not print a fourth-quarter column |

| Balance sheets | December 31, 2024 and 2025 (10-K page:77); June 30, 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:2); March 31, 2026 and September 30, 2025 in the matching 10-Qs | Dated point-in-time; September 30, 2026 is not supplied |
| Cash interest and taxes | 10-K page:80 (annual); Q2 10-Q page:6 (six months) | Includes discontinued operations in cash flows (Q2 10-Q page:7) |
### Debt, liquidity and covenant evidence located (no calculation)

- Instruments at June 30, 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:15): term loan facility due August 2028; 7.875% Senior Secured Notes due April 2030; 7.125% Senior Secured Notes due February 2031; 7.500% Senior Secured Notes due March 2033; 7.750% Senior Notes due April 2028; 7.500% Senior Notes due June 2029; finance leases; the receivables-based and revolving facilities are shown with no balance, both maturing June 2030.

- Facility availability at June 30, 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:33): revolving facility limit $100.0 million, receivables-based facility limit $200.0 million, letters of credit $7.0 million and $87.6 million, excess availability $93.0 million and $112.4 million. The revolver letter of credit related to Spain and "was canceled" on August 4, 2026 (page:34). The receivables-based limit is capped by a borrowing base (page:34).
- Maturity schedule at December 31, 2025 by year is printed (10-K page:117). A June 30, 2026 schedule is not printed; the Q2 10-Q says the next significant maturities are in 2028 (page:32).

- Springing covenant: first lien net leverage ratio of less than 7.10 to 1.00, applicable only if the revolver is drawn or undrawn letters of credit exceed $10 million; "these conditions were not met and the covenant was not in effect" at June 30, 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:34; 10-K page:109 for the full carve-outs). The reported ratio is therefore not presented. The receivables-based facility has a fixed charge coverage test that applies only in a Covenant Trigger Period (10-K page:106).
- Compliance: "the Company was in compliance with all covenants" at June 30, 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:16).

- Non-debt claims located: operating leases (10-K page:117, maturities table), non-lease non-cancelable contracts and capital expenditure commitments (10-K page:118), surety bonds and bank guarantees (Q2 10-Q page:16), asset retirement obligations (10-K page:125). A search for pension, retiree medical, factoring and supply-chain finance in the 10-K found no program of the issuer; the only pension reference is a reclassification of pension-related translation losses on sold businesses (10-K page:78). Treat these as not found in the supplied text, not as confirmed absent.
### Pending merger and debt actions at the latest filing

- Merger Agreement dated February 9, 2026, $2.43 per share in cash, stockholder approval on May 12, 2026, Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period expired April 9, 2026, closing "expected to close by the end of the third quarter of 2026" subject to remaining conditions including review by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (Q2 10-Q page:8, page:9).
- Termination fees: company pays Parent $39.8 million in specified circumstances; Parent pays the company $92.9 million in other circumstances (Q2 10-Q page:8).

- Debt documents: consent solicitations completed April and May 2026; supplemental indentures and amendments make the merger not a change of control; those for the senior secured notes and the Senior Secured Credit Agreement are "effective but will become operative only upon consummation of the Merger"; the receivables-based amendment becomes effective on consummation and would extend maturity to five years from closing and raise commitments from $200.0 million to $250.0 million (Q2 10-Q page:16, page:17).
- Conditional notices of redemption were issued for the 7.750% Senior Notes due 2028 and 7.500% Senior Notes due 2029, conditional on the merger closing (Q2 10-Q page:17).

- Spain sale: price approximately $132.3 million, completed August 4, 2026, net proceeds subject to adjustments and fees, intended to "further reduce our outstanding debt, subject to the outcome of the Merger" (Q2 10-Q page:22, page:33); completion and price are in Note 2 (page:9). The 10-K had expected closing in the first half of 2026 (page:4); the sale completed after that window.

- Consequence for readiness: the supplied set describes these events as pending. Any statement about the merger closing, notes redeemed, the receivables-based amendment taking effect or Spain proceeds applied to debt would be an inference, and downstream modules must label it Not supplied.
### Conflicts, differences and source-quality notes
| Item | Locators | Downstream effect |

| Cash of $202.3 million in MD&A versus $192.1 million on the balance sheet | Q2 10-Q page:32 and page:2 | Not a conflict: MD&A includes $10.1 million held by discontinued operations in Spain (page:32, page:10). Use the labelled figure. |
| Credit-facility table totals differ by $0.1 million from the sum of its columns | Q2 10-Q page:33, footnote on page:34 "Due to rounding" | Presentation rounding only. Use facility-level figures. |

| Revenue mix between contracts with customers and leases shifts sharply year over year | Q2 10-Q page:14, page:15 (explained as changed contract terms, not a change in volume) | Do not use the mix as a trend in underlying business without the stated explanation. |
| Q4 2025 not printed in the 10-K | Q4 release page:1 | The discrete quarter comes from a release, not a filed statement. |
| Three-month and six-month 2025 columns are on a recast continuing basis | Q2 10-Q page:3, page:7 | Do not mix with pre-recast original reports. |
| Buyer description differs in wording | 10-K page:4; Q2 10-Q page:8 | Carry both wordings; do not resolve the TWG Global role from these sources. |
| 10-K said Spain sale expected in first half of 2026; it closed August 4, 2026 | 10-K page:4; Q2 10-Q page:9 | Timeline drift is a fact, not an error; no other conflict found. |
### Analytical read-through

- Usable coverage: the 10-K, three 10-Qs and three releases together cover audited FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023, every quarter from the first quarter of 2025 through the second quarter of 2026 on one continuing-operations basis, and the two segments, digital and total revenue, site lease expense, debt by instrument, facility availability, cash interest and the springing covenant.

- Strongest contrary evidence: the filings describe a take-private merger whose closing, debt amendments and note redemptions were all still pending on the last supplied date. The source risk is that the capital structure in the supplied balance sheet may not be the structure that exists at the cutoff. The downstream consequence is that leverage, interest burden and maturity profile are valid at June 30, 2026 only, and a user of CP-2 must not present them as the structure at the cutoff.

- Source risk mechanism, legal documents: the notes, credit agreements and their amendments are described only in the issuer's own notes and exhibit lists. The covenant and change-of-control mechanics therefore rest on management summary. The consequence is that CP-2 can report the stated covenant level and compliance statement but cannot test definitions, baskets or guarantor release terms.
- Source risk mechanism, guarantor perimeter: guarantors are "certain" domestic subsidiaries with no list. The consequence is that structural subordination and guarantor coverage cannot be assessed.

- What cannot proceed: any statement about events after August 5, 2026; document-level legal interpretation; guarantor-level analysis; a covenant headroom figure (the test was not in effect, so no ratio is printed); post-merger capital structure.

- Next evidence action: supply filings dated August 6, 2026 to November 5, 2026, including any report on the merger closing or termination, redemption of the senior unsecured notes, the quarter ended September 30, 2026 if filed by the cutoff, and the Form 10-K/A. Supply the indentures, the Senior Secured Credit Agreement with its seventh amendment, the receivables-based credit agreement with its third amendment, and the Merger Agreement, which the exhibit lists cite.
## Calculations
No new calculation is made; CP-0 does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. The checks below are coverage counts and footing checks of printed totals, shown with their inputs.

- Page chunks retained: 145 + 48 + 36 + 39 + 16 + 12 + 12 = 308 of 308 pages across the seven sources. Every page is retained text; none is an evidenced exclusion. Coverage of the document universe is not proven by this count.

- Debt table footing, December 31, 2025 (10-K page:101), thousands of USD: 425,000 + 865,000 + 1,150,000 + 900,000 + 899,311 + 905,950 + 3,636 - 3,605 - 42,299 = 5,102,993, equal to the printed "Total debt".
- Issuer-printed net debt check (Q2 release page:6): 5,107,629 - 192,138 = 4,915,491, equal to the printed figure. This is a footing check of an issuer presentation only.

- Facility columns, June 30, 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:33), millions: letters of credit 7.0 + 87.6 = 94.6 against 94.5 printed; excess availability 93.0 + 112.4 = 205.4 against 205.5 printed. The footnote attributes the difference to rounding (page:34).

- Annual to quarterly series, revenue, thousands of USD: nine months 2025 of 1,142,625 (Q3 2025 10-Q page:3) plus fourth quarter 2025 of 461,515 (Q4 release page:1) = 1,604,140, equal to the printed FY2025 revenue (10-K page:78). This is a footing check on source consistency, not a normalized series.
## Gaps

## Findings
### Reader summary

| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Operating lease liabilities of 1,361.9 sit outside the debt figure. | Fixed lease obligations rank alongside debt service and are not captured in the debt ratios. | High |
### Financial base view

Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. is a highly leveraged, now almost entirely U.S. out-of-home advertiser whose reported earnings are improving while its debt stack is unchanged. On the issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA of 544.3 for the twelve months to June 30, 2026 (FY2025 of 504.8 plus H1 2026 of 247.3 less H1 2025 of 207.8), debt principal including finance leases of 5,148.8 is 9.46x and, net of 192.1 of continuing cash, 9.11x, down from 10.20x and 9.82x at FY2025. Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest paid of 390.1 only 1.40x, against 1.28x for FY2025 and 1.09x for FY2024. Revenue for the twelve months is 1,679.1 against 1,604.1 for FY2025, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin is 32.4%. Free cash flow, defined here as operating cash flow of 160.4 less capital expenditures of 76.1, is 84.3; both inputs include discontinued operations. Debt principal barely changed between December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026: every note and term-loan balance is identical, and only finance leases moved, down 0.1. So the leverage improvement is earnings-led. The structure is 3,340.0 of first-priority secured debt (a 425.0 term loan and 2,915.0 of senior secured notes), 1,805.3 of senior unsecured notes due 2028 and 2029, and undrawn facilities; the secured share of principal is high, and the unsecured notes are effectively subordinated to it. Liquidity is 192.1 of cash and 205.5 of excess availability under a 100.0 revolving facility and a 200.0 receivables-based facility, both maturing June 12, 2030. The next significant maturities are in 2028, when 899.3 of 7.750% senior notes and the 425.0 term loan fall due, and the company has issued conditional redemption notices for the 2028 and 2029 unsecured notes, with conditions that include the merger closing. Operating lease liabilities of 1,361.9 and 877.6 of non-lease non-cancelable contracts at December 31, 2025 sit outside debt. Three qualifications bound this view. First, Adjusted EBITDA is the issuer's non-GAAP measure and is stated after site lease expense; the covenant EBITDA is not supplied. Second, cash-flow figures include the Spain business that was held for sale and the 2025 cash flows of businesses sold in 2025. Third, nothing after August 5, 2026 is supplied, so the merger, the redemption notices and the use of Spain sale proceeds, which are described as pending, cannot be reflected.

| Revolving Credit Facility | — (undrawn) | June 2030; commitment 100,000 | Company as borrower; first-priority lien pari passu with the term loan and secured notes | S4 page:15, page:33; S1 page:107, page:108 |

| Term Loan Facility | 425,000 | August 2028 (springing earlier date if certain secured notes remain outstanding); floating rate, Term SOFR plus an Applicable Rate that is not printed | Company as borrower; guaranteed by certain domestic subsidiaries; first-priority | S4 page:15; S1 page:107, page:108 |

| 7.875% Senior Secured Notes | 865,000 | April 1, 2030; semi-annual interest | Company; guaranteed by certain wholly-owned domestic subsidiaries; first-priority on the notes collateral | S4 page:15; S1 page:110 |
| 7.125% Senior Secured Notes | 1,150,000 | February 15, 2031; interest February 15 and August 15 | As above | S4 page:15; S1 page:112 |
| 7.500% Senior Secured Notes | 900,000 | March 15, 2033; interest March 15 and September 15 | As above | S4 page:15; S1 page:112, page:113 |

| 7.750% Senior Notes | 899,311 | April 15, 2028; interest April 15 and October 15 | Company; senior unsecured guarantees from certain domestic subsidiaries; effectively subordinated to secured debt and structurally subordinated to non-guarantors | S4 page:15; S1 page:114 |

The principal amounts of the six notes and term loan, and the finance leases, add to 5,148,750 (C3), and the carrying total ties after discount and fees (C9). Notes repurchased in 2025 (95.7 million of the 7.750% notes and 134.1 million of the 7.500% notes) are held by the company and not cancelled; the table shows balances net of them (S1 page:102). About 8% of debt was variable rate at December 31, 2025 (S1 page:73) and the weighted average cost of debt was 7.6% (S1 page:73). Amendments and conditional redemption notices tied to the pending merger are described under Subsequent events and pending items.
### Liquidity
| Component | Amount (US$m) | Source |
| Cash and cash equivalents, continuing operations, June 30, 2026 | 192.1 | S4 page:2 |
| Cash held by discontinued operations in Spain (excluded) | 10.1 | S4 page:10 |
| Revolving facility: limit 100.0, letters of credit 7.0, excess availability | 93.0 | S4 page:33 |
| Receivables-based facility: limit 200.0, letters of credit 87.6, excess availability | 112.4 | S4 page:33 |
| Total excess availability as printed | 205.5 | S4 page:33 |
| Borrowings outstanding on either facility | None drawn (printed as a dash) | S4 page:33 |

Of the 192.1 of continuing cash, 5.5 is held by continuing subsidiaries outside the U.S. (S4 page:32). The company states "We believe our sources of liquidity will be sufficient to meet our cash requirements for at least the next 12 months" (S4 page:29). Both facilities mature June 12, 2030 (S4 page:33), so no facility expires within twelve months. The receivables-based availability depends on a borrowing base that fluctuates with receivables (S4 page:34), and its fixed charge coverage test applies only in a Covenant Trigger Period (S1 page:106). Surety bonds of 42.6 and bank guarantees of 10.9 were outstanding at June 30, 2026, partly supported by 2.7 of cash collateral (S4 page:16). The company expects cash interest of about 197 million in the second half of 2026 and about 394 million in 2027 on June 30, 2026 debt (S4 page:32). Net proceeds of the Spain sale are not in the balance sheet and are subject to adjustments and fees (S4 page:9).
### Claims outside the debt figure
| Claim | Amount | Inside or outside debt | Source |

| Operating lease liabilities, current and non-current, June 30, 2026 | 1,361.9 US$m (134.4 current) | Outside; at December 31, 2025 undiscounted lease payments were 2,218.6 and the weighted-average discount rate 7.88% | S4 page:2; S1 page:117 |
| Non-lease non-cancelable contracts, December 31, 2025 | 877.6 US$m | Outside; payments by year printed | S1 page:118 |
| Capital expenditure commitments, December 31, 2025 | 152.7 US$m | Outside | S1 page:118 |
| Finance lease obligations | 3.5 US$m | Inside the principal figure used here | S4 page:15 |
| Surety bonds and bank guarantees, June 30, 2026 | 42.6 and 10.9 US$m | Off balance sheet; a portion relates to Spain | S4 page:16 |
| Asset retirement obligations, December 31, 2025 | 24.6 US$m | Inside other liabilities | S1 page:125 |
| Pension and retiree medical | Not found in the supplied sources for continuing operations | Not supplied | S1 page:78 (pension appears only as a reclassification on sold businesses) |
| Factoring and supply-chain finance | Not found in the supplied sources | Not supplied | Keyword search of all seven sources |
| Litigation | Ordinary-course claims, accrued where probable; no amount printed | Not quantified | S4 page:17 |
| Merger termination fee payable by the company in specified circumstances | 39.8 US$m | Contingent | S4 page:8 |
### Covenants

- Springing financial covenant (Senior Secured Credit Agreement): a first lien net leverage ratio of less than 7.10 to 1.00, applying only if the revolver has an outstanding balance or undrawn letters of credit under it exceed 10 million; "these conditions were not met and the covenant was not in effect" at June 30, 2026 (S4 page:34), with further carve-outs described at S1 page:109. The reported ratio is therefore not printed, and headroom is Not calculable from the sources.

- Receivables-based facility: a fixed charge coverage ratio of no less than 1.00 to 1.00 applies only in a Covenant Trigger Period; it did not apply for the four quarters ended December 31, 2025 (S1 page:106). A June 30, 2026 statement of its status is Not supplied.
- Compliance: the company states it "was in compliance with all covenants contained in its debt agreements" at June 30, 2026 (S4 page:16).

- Indenture covenants limit debt, liens, restricted payments, investments, asset sales and affiliate transactions (S1 page:111). Definitions and baskets are in executed documents that are not supplied.
- The secured-debt ratio in the metrics table is first-priority principal over Adjusted EBITDA. It is not the covenant measure, whose EBITDA and net debt definitions are not supplied.
### Subsequent events and pending items

- Spain sale: completed August 4, 2026 for approximately 132.3 million; net proceeds subject to adjustments and fees; intended to reduce debt "subject to the outcome of the Merger" (S4 page:22). Not in the June 30, 2026 balance sheet. Illustrative sensitivity: if the full price reduced debt principal, total debt over LTM Adjusted EBITDA would be 9.22x (C10); the net amount and its application are not supplied.

- Pending merger: Madison Parent Inc. to acquire the company at 2.43 per share in cash; closing expected by the end of the third quarter of 2026; stockholders approved on May 12, 2026 (S4 page:8). No source says whether it closed.

- Debt amendments: supplemental indentures and credit-agreement amendments provide that the merger is not a change of control; those for the secured notes and the Senior Secured Credit Agreement are effective but operative only on closing; the receivables-based amendment would extend its maturity to five years from closing and raise commitments from 200.0 to 250.0 (S4 page:16, page:17).

- Conditional redemption notices were issued for the 7.750% and 7.500% Senior Notes, conditional on the merger closing (S4 page:17). If effected, 1,805.3 of unsecured principal would be redeemed (C3), but the funding source is not supplied.
- The 10-K recorded the August 2025 refinancing of 2,000.0 of 5.125% and 9.000% secured notes into 7.125% and 7.500% secured notes, with a 43.8 loss on extinguishment (S1 page:102).
### Definition and basis risks

1. Adjusted EBITDA is the issuer's non-GAAP measure: loss from continuing operations plus tax, non-operating items, other operating expense, depreciation and amortization, share-based compensation, and restructuring and other costs (S7 page:7). It is after site lease expense, which sits in direct operating expenses (S4 page:24) and includes minimum guaranteed payments and revenue-sharing rent (S4 page:13). Covenant EBITDA is not supplied.

2. Total debt used here is principal including finance leases before discount and fees. The issuer's printed total and net debt are on carrying value (S7 page:6); the difference at June 30, 2026 is 41.1 (C3).
3. The FY2024 debt includes the CCIBV term loan, which belonged to businesses later sold; FY2024 leverage is shown with a sensitivity excluding it (C3).

4. Cash flow figures include discontinued operations (S4 page:7, page:8), while Adjusted EBITDA is continuing operations only. Trailing operating cash flow and capital expenditures include Spain in all periods and businesses sold in 2025 in FY2025 and H1 2025.
5. The Q3 2025 Adjusted EBITDA is derived from three printed figures and not printed in the supplied set.
6. The revenue mix between contracts with customers and leases changed sharply year over year because of changed contract terms (S4 page:15); that does not change total revenue.
7. Net income and cash flow for H1 2025 include large one-time items from the 2025 disposals (S4 page:11), so the trailing figures rely on continuing operations.
8. All balances are at June 30, 2026, before the Spain sale and the pending merger-related actions.
## Calculations
All inputs are printed figures cited above, in USD thousands unless stated. Results are shown in US$m to one decimal (ratios to two decimals), rounded half up.
C1. LTM to June 30, 2026 equals FY2025 plus H1 2026 less H1 2025.
- Total Segment Adjusted EBITDA: 595,120 + 299,336 - 253,561 = 640,895.
- Adjusted Corporate expenses: 90,330 + 52,057 - 45,746 = 96,641.
- Loss from continuing operations: (103,747) + (59,449) - (48,971) = (114,225).
C3. Leverage. Principal including finance leases equals the sum of the term loan, the five notes and finance leases.
- Carrying versus principal at June 30, 2026: 5,148,750 - 5,107,629 = 41,121, equal to discount 2,967 plus fees 38,154.
C4. Cover.

- Coupon cross-check: 865,000 x 7.875% + 1,150,000 x 7.125% + 900,000 x 7.5% + 899,311 x 7.75% + 905,950 x 7.5% = 68,118.75 + 81,937.5 + 67,500 + 69,696.5 + 67,946.25 = 355,199.0, of the issuer's expected 2027 cash interest of about 394,000 (S4 page:32). The remainder of about 38,801 covers the floating term loan, fees and facility costs; the term-loan margin is not printed, so this is an upper-bound residual, not a rate.

C7. Free cash flow equals operating cash flow less capital expenditures: LTM 160,374 - 76,122 = 84,252; FY2025 114,860 - 82,879 = 31,981; FY2024 79,746 - 142,395 = -62,649; H1 2026 47,840 - 35,323 = 12,517; H1 2025 2,326 - 42,080 = -39,754. Both inputs include discontinued operations.

C8. Lease-adjusted leverage, indicative. FY2025: (5,148,897 + 1,367,706) / (504,790 + 273,448) = 6,516,603 / 778,238 = 8.37, where 273,448 is operating lease expense of continuing operations (S1 page:117). FY2024: (5,703,974 + 1,362,222) / (475,758 + 251,229) = 7,066,196 / 726,987 = 9.72. The LTM value is Not supplied because interim operating lease expense is not printed.
C9. Tie-outs, all equal to printed totals.
- Capital expenditures: FY2025 continuing 61,784 + discontinued 21,095 = 82,879; H1 2026 29,735 + 5,588 = 35,323.

- Quarterly revenue: 405,637 + 461,515 + 373,864 + 438,040 = 1,679,056, equal to the LTM revenue in C1. Quarterly Adjusted EBITDA: 132,515 + 164,460 + 103,847 + 143,432 = 544,254, equal to the LTM figure; and 103,847 + 143,432 = 247,279.

C10. Spain sensitivity (illustrative): (5,148,750 - 132,300) / 544,254 = 9.22. It uses the gross price of approximately 132.3 million, ignores adjustments, fees and cash that leaves with the business, and assumes full application to debt, which the company ties to the merger outcome.

C11. Direction checks. Leverage 10.20 at FY2025 and 9.46 at LTM: lower (C3). Debt principal 5,148,897 at December 31, 2025 and 5,148,750 at June 30, 2026: essentially unchanged, down 147 (finance leases 3,636 to 3,489). Adjusted EBITDA rose from 504,790 (FY2025) to 544,254 (LTM). Cash interest cover rose from 1.28 to 1.40 (C4). Cash rose from 190,022 to 192,138.
## Gaps
- Undrawn facilities at December 31, 2024: Not supplied. The FY2025 annual report prints excess availability only at December 31, 2025; the liquidity chart carries Not supplied for that row.

- Covenant levels and headroom: the springing ratio was not in effect and is not printed; covenant EBITDA and net debt definitions are in executed documents that are not supplied. Headroom is Not calculable.
- Operating lease expense for interim periods: not printed in the 10-Qs, so a trailing lease-adjusted leverage is Not supplied.
- Term loan margin: the Applicable Rate is not printed, so floating interest cannot be rebuilt from coupons; the coupon cross-check leaves an unexplained residual (C4).
- Adjusted EBITDA is issuer-defined and non-GAAP; no covenant or lender-defined EBITDA is supplied. Q3 2025 Adjusted EBITDA is derived, not printed.

- Cash-flow and cash-interest figures include discontinued operations; the continuing-operations split of operating cash flow and cash interest is Not supplied. Capital expenditures of continuing operations are printed and shown separately.
- FY2024 debt includes the CCIBV term loan of sold businesses; a continuing-only FY2024 debt figure is shown by sensitivity only.
- Guarantor and non-guarantor financial information is Not supplied (CP-0); structural subordination of the unsecured notes cannot be quantified.

- Everything after August 5, 2026 is Not supplied, including the merger outcome, redemption of the unsecured notes, effect of the amendments, the net Spain proceeds and their use, and a September 30, 2026 balance sheet.
- Pension, retiree medical, factoring and supply-chain finance programs: not found in the supplied text; treated as Not supplied rather than zero.
- Ratings, market quotes, peers and valuation inputs are blank in the context; no market value of debt beyond the printed approximation of 5.3 billion at June 30, 2026 (S4 page:16).
## Next module

CP-1A should take the business and transaction facts from the pending-merger items above (merger at 2.43 per share, closing expected by the end of the third quarter of 2026 but not confirmed in the supplied set, termination fees of 39.8 and 92.9, amendments operative only on closing, conditional redemption notices), the Spain sale completed on August 4, 2026, the 2025 disposals and refinancing history, the segment revenue and Segment Adjusted EBITDA table, and the digital revenue share. CP-2 should read leverage as 9.46x total debt and 9.11x net debt on trailing issuer-defined Adjusted EBITDA, cash interest cover of 1.40x, first-priority secured leverage of 6.14x, and 5,148.8 of principal that did not change in 2026, together with the operating leases outside debt, the absence of a printed covenant ratio, the pending merger, the exposure of the unsecured notes to structural subordination, and the stale-date restriction. CP-5 should trace each calculated figure to the printed inputs in `## Calculations`, check that no trailing metric uses a figure dated after August 5, 2026, and flag that Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Corporate expenses, AFFO and net debt come from releases or issuer non-GAAP presentations, while statement figures come from the filings.

## Request

- Issuer: Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. (issuer id `cco`, NYSE: CCO), consolidated, as of 2026-11-05 (information cutoff 2026-11-05). Pathway `credit_snapshot`, module CP-1A (business and transaction context). Reporting currency USD (context).

- Reader question: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to a creditor? Decision drivers: transaction and ownership structure; business and operating model; credit-relevant history or change.

- Perimeter: the continuing operations of the consolidated group (America and Airports segments, with Singapore in Other). The Spain business is a discontinued operation held for sale at June 30, 2026 and sold on August 4, 2026.
- Information boundary: the latest supplied documents are dated August 5, 2026 (CP-0). Anything after that date, including the outcome of the pending merger, is Not supplied, not absent.

- Locator convention: "S1 page:14" is the retained text chunk numbered 14 of source S1, not a printed page. Quotes are exact substrings of the named chunk once line breaks are read as spaces and curly quotes as straight quotes. Figures are in USD; amounts quoted from the statements are in thousands where marked, otherwise in USD millions as the filings print them, and they agree with the CP-1 handoff where they overlap.
- Category tags used on every fact row: Documentary Fact; Management Language; Analyst Interpretation; Insufficient Information.
- Scope limits: no peer ranking, no instrument recommendation, no recovery conclusion. External material is labelled as such. Governance is assessed at issuer level only, from documented actions.

### Run settings (not issuer evidence)

Context file sha256 de960bbc410d3388b8cf7496a6e161733b9fd5ffc09b25a54e06ffd5d05f0294. It names the issuer, the as-of date, USD, the sector label "Services-Advertising" and a listed-equity ticker. Sponsor, parent, guarantors, ratings, deal terms and quotes are blank, and blank is not zero.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Clear Channel Outdoor is a U.S. roadside and airport advertiser with long-dated site contracts and heavy fixed rent. A take-private merger at 2.43 per share is pending, and its status after August 5, 2026 is unknown. | Medium | No source after August 5, 2026, and the merger agreement, debt documents and ownership table are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The merger agreement allows termination if the merger has not closed by November 9, 2026, extendable to February 9, 2027 if regulatory approvals are outstanding. | The cutoff falls four days before the first outside date, so the owner at the cutoff cannot be confirmed. | High |

| Amendments to the secured notes and credit agreement make the merger not a change of control, but they become operative only on closing. | Lender and noteholder protections depend on whether the merger closes; terms of consent payments are not supplied. | High |

| Airports Segment Adjusted EBITDA margin was 25.3% in H1 2026 against 41.0% for America, because airport site lease expense was 59.2% of revenue. | Airport growth adds fixed minimum-guarantee rent, so margins and cash flow are more exposed there than in roadside. | Medium |

| Substantially all international operations were sold in 2025 and 2026, and sale proceeds and cash reduced indebtedness by about 605 million in 2025. | The business is now almost wholly U.S., with few international assets left to sell as a deleveraging source. | Medium |

| Beneficial ownership is not in the supplied sources because the annual report defers it to an amendment that is not supplied. | Control, sponsor identity and any equity support after closing cannot be assessed. | High |
### Business and transaction view

Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. is a listed U.S. out-of-home advertising operator with no controlling holder identified in the supplied sources, whose creditor story is a simplified, almost entirely domestic business sitting under a heavy, mostly unchanged debt stack while a take-private merger is pending. The operating base is roadside billboards and street furniture in the America segment and airport concessions in the Airports segment, together more than 64,500 displays at June 30, 2026, with digital displays a small share of inventory but a large share of revenue. Revenue is sold in short periods, mostly four weeks in roadside, against site leases and municipal and airport concessions that run for years with minimum guaranteed payments, so revenue visibility is short while the main cost is fixed or semi-fixed. That asymmetry is sharper in Airports, where site lease expense was 59.2% of revenue in H1 2026 against 31.3% in America (C1), so airport growth carries more fixed rent. Seasonality is steady: first quarter weakest and fourth quarter strongest. The credit-relevant history is a multi-year exit from international markets, completed with the sale of Spain on August 4, 2026, and a sequence of refinancings that moved secured maturities out to 2031 and 2033 while leaving the unsecured notes in 2028 and 2029. The transaction that matters most is the merger signed on February 9, 2026 with Madison Parent Inc., at 2.43 per share in cash, approved by stockholders on May 12, 2026 and expected, per the latest filing, to close by the end of the third quarter of 2026. The merger agreement lets either party terminate if closing has not happened by November 9, 2026, extendable to February 9, 2027 if regulatory approvals are outstanding, so the cutoff of November 5, 2026 falls four days before the first outside date, and the supplied sources do not say whether closing occurred. Debt amendments and conditional redemption notices tied to the merger exist, but they are described as pending. Ownership of the equity after closing, the merger financing, and the executed debt documents are not supplied. Documented issuer actions so far are mostly supportive or neutral for creditors, with disposal proceeds applied to debt and no dividends; none of the creditor-adverse actions in the method's checklist is documented in the supplied filings, which is a statement about the sources, not a finding about the executed documents.
### Company and operating model
| Area | Fact | Category | Source | Creditor mechanism |

| Core activity and revenue model | Sells advertising on printed and digital out-of-home displays: roadside billboards and street furniture (America) and airport displays (Airports). Most America advertising is sold in four-week periods; Airports contracts typically run four weeks to one year. Q2 2026 revenue of 438,040 thousand split 388,985 thousand contracts with customers and 49,055 thousand leases | Documentary Fact | S1 page:12; S1 page:15; S4 page:14 | Short selling periods give little contracted revenue visibility, while costs are committed for years |

| Segment mix | America was 75% and Airports 25% of 2025 revenue from continuing operations. In H1 2026 America revenue was 602,803 thousand, Airports 208,827 thousand and Other 274 thousand | Documentary Fact | S1 page:11; S1 page:12; S4 page:12 | Roadside is the cash engine; Airports is the faster-growing, lower-margin segment |

| Footprint | At December 31, 2025: 48,220 America displays across 28 U.S. DMAs and 12,782 Airports displays of which 2,583 digital; operations in 81 DMAs including 43 of the top 50. At June 30, 2026: 64,521 displays in total, 5,145 of them digital | Documentary Fact | S1 page:11; S1 page:14; S1 page:15; S7 page:3 | Dense, permit-protected inventory is hard to replicate; permits and site rights are the asset base |

| Product mix | Bulletins were 76% of America revenue in 2025, posters 11%, spectaculars and wallscapes 5%, street furniture 3% | Documentary Fact | S1 page:12 | Revenue leans on large-format billboards, which the company says carry higher margins |

| Digital | Digital assets were "approximately 8% of our inventory but generated 44% of our revenue" in 2025; 71 large-format digital billboards were added in 2025; digital revenue in Q2 2026 was 195,426 thousand, 44.6% of revenue | Documentary Fact | S1 page:8; S4 page:24 | Digital conversion raises yield per structure but needs permits and capital spending |

| Customers and sales channel | No single advertiser was a material portion of consolidated revenue in 2025. National sales were 35.5% of America and 62.0% of Airports revenue in 2025; 33.9% and 57.8% in Q2 2026 | Documentary Fact | S1 page:11; S1 page:60; S1 page:61; S4 page:27; S4 page:28 | Diversified advertisers limit single-name risk; national budgets are cyclical and agency driven |

| Market concentration | Los Angeles was 12% of 2025 America revenue, New York 9% and San Francisco/Bay Area 7%. Q2 2026 growth cites the San Francisco/Bay Area and San Francisco International Airport with technology advertisers | Documentary Fact | S1 page:13; S4 page:24; S4 page:27; S4 page:28 | Sector and metro concentration (technology demand, large coastal markets) raises sensitivity to a local ad downturn |

| Contract tenor | Street furniture contracts with municipal and transit authorities generally run five to fifteen years; airport contracts five to ten years, each with a minimum fee and/or revenue share; roadside site leases generally one to twenty years | Documentary Fact | S1 page:16 | Long contracts lock in inventory but also fixed minimum payments |

| Cost structure | Site lease expense was 163,275 thousand of direct operating expenses of 196,178 thousand in Q2 2026. The company calls site lease payments its "most significant recurring operating cash requirement" | Documentary Fact | S4 page:24; S4 page:3; S4 page:30 | Rent dominates costs, so a revenue shortfall flows into margin quickly |

| Airport minimum guarantees | Airports site lease expense rose 12.0% in Q2 2026, reflecting "higher minimum guaranteed payments under certain airport contracts" and the renewal with the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority, whose agreement carries 412.0 million of non-lease non-cancelable payments over 15 years | Documentary Fact | S4 page:28; S1 page:119 | Fixed airport rent rises with prior-period performance and persists if traffic or demand falls |

| Large contract | A 15-year contract with the New York Metropolitan Transportation Authority, effective November 1, 2024, has total undiscounted minimum lease payments of 390.0 million | Documentary Fact | S1 page:118 | A large fixed commitment inside the lease liabilities that sit outside the debt figure |

| Segment margins | Segment Adjusted EBITDA margin was 41.0% in America and 25.3% in Airports in H1 2026 (C1) | Analyst Interpretation | S4 page:12 | Airport growth dilutes consolidated margin unless site lease growth slows |

| Seasonality and cyclicality | Performance is typically weakest in the first quarter and strongest in the fourth; advertising spending generally correlates with gross domestic product | Documentary Fact | S1 page:16; S4 page:22; S4 page:23 | Liquidity is tightest in the first quarter; a recession hits both revenue and covenant-style metrics |

| Event-driven demand | Revenue growth in Q2 2026 reflected increased advertising activity associated with the 2026 FIFA World Cup, and in H1 2026 Super Bowl LX | Documentary Fact | S4 page:24 | Part of the 2026 growth is event driven and may not repeat |

| Capital spending | Capital expenditures of continuing operations were 61,784 thousand in FY2025 and 29,735 thousand in H1 2026; maintenance capital expenditures were 24,307 thousand in FY2025 | Documentary Fact | S1 page:99; S4 page:13; S5 page:10 | Capital needs are modest relative to EBITDA, so cash flow depends mainly on rent and interest |

| Working capital | Deferred revenue was 102,730 thousand at June 30, 2026 against 75,437 thousand at December 31, 2025 | Documentary Fact | S4 page:2 | Advance billings fund operations seasonally and reverse in weaker quarters |

| Competition and regulation | Competitors include Lamar Advertising Company and Outfront Media Inc.; billboard permits are regulated by state and local law and the Highway Beautification Act. ### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The pending transaction is the take-private merger. On February 9, 2026 the company agreed to be acquired by an investor consortium of affiliates and/or certain investment funds advised by Mubadala Capital through Madison Parent Inc. and Madison Merger Sub Inc., with Merger Sub merging into the company, which would survive as a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent (S1 page:4; S4 page:8). Holders of common stock would receive 2.43 per share in cash. The Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period expired on April 9, 2026 and stockholders approved the agreement on May 12, 2026 (S4 page:8). The latest filing says closing is expected by the end of the third quarter of 2026, subject to remaining customary conditions including review by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (S4 page:8). The annual report adds termination rights if the merger is not consummated on or before November 9, 2026, extendable to February 9, 2027 if requisite regulatory approvals are not obtained, a termination fee payable by the company of 39.8 million, or 19.9 million during the go-shop period, and a fee payable by Parent of 92.9 million under certain other circumstances (S1 page:24; S1 page:53; S1 page:54). The company has represented that the buyer has sufficient funds, but it also warns that the equity and debt financing contemplated by the merger agreement must be funded or closed (S1 page:24). The financing amounts, the sources of the buyer's equity and the post-closing capital structure are Not supplied. Until closing, the agreement restricts the company from incurring certain debt, paying dividends, settling certain proceedings and incurring certain capital expenditures without the buyer's written consent (S1 page:25). The first outside date, November 9, 2026, falls four days after the cutoff of November 5, 2026, and nothing in the supplied sources reports whether the merger closed or the dates moved.

The merger has direct debt consequences, all described as pending at August 5, 2026. In April 2026 the company completed consent solicitations with holders of its senior secured notes and with the lenders under its credit agreement, and in May 2026 with the lenders under its receivables-based credit agreement, entering into supplemental indentures and amendments dated April 9, April 10 and May 15, 2026 (S4 page:8; S4 page:9; S4 page:38; S4 page:39). These provide that the merger will not constitute a change of control under the debt documents; the supplemental indentures and the credit agreement amendment are effective but become operative only on consummation of the merger, and cease to be effective if it is not completed (S4 page:16). The receivables-based amendment, when effective, would extend the maturity of that facility to five years from the merger, raise revolving commitments from 200.0 million to 250.0 million, broaden the borrowing base and permit qualified securitisation financings (S4 page:16; S4 page:17). The company has also issued conditional notices of redemption for the 7.750% Senior Notes due 2028 and the 7.500% Senior Notes due 2029, conditional on closing (S4 page:17). Together these actions would remove the 2028 and 2029 unsecured maturities and keep the secured notes outstanding with changed change-of-control terms, but the consent terms, the redemption price and the source of redemption funds are Not supplied, and the executed supplemental indentures and amendments are cited in the exhibit list but not supplied (S4 page:38; S4 page:39). No new debt was issued in the first half of 2026: the six-month cash flow shows 145 thousand of debt repayments and no issuance line (S4 page:5).

Earlier new debt issues explain the current stack. In March 2024 the company issued 865.0 million of 7.875% Senior Secured Notes due 2030 and used part of the proceeds to prepay 835.0 million of its term loan, refinancing the remaining 425.0 million and extending its maturity to August 2028 (S1 page:69; S1 page:107). On August 4, 2025 it issued 1,150.0 million of 7.125% Senior Secured Notes due 2031 and 900.0 million of 7.500% Senior Secured Notes due 2033, and with cash on hand redeemed 1,250.0 million of 5.125% and 750.0 million of 9.000% senior secured notes; it paid 62.0 million of accrued interest, a 36.1 million redemption premium and 26.3 million of other fees, and recognised a 43.8 million loss on extinguishment (S1 page:69; S1 page:102). In June 2025 it extended the revolving and receivables-based facilities to June 12, 2030, reduced the revolver from 115.8 million to 100.0 million and raised the receivables-based facility from 175.0 million to 200.0 million (S1 page:102). In the second quarter of 2025 it repurchased 95.7 million of 7.750% and 134.1 million of 7.500% senior notes in the open market for 203.4 million including accrued interest and fees, recognising a gain of 28.8 million; the repurchased notes are held by the company and not cancelled (S1 page:102). The debt register, maturities and liquidity are in the CP-1 handoff: principal is 5,148.8 million at June 30, 2026 and no significant maturities fall before 2028.

The disposal programme is the other transaction thread. The company sold Switzerland, Italy and France in 2023, Mexico, Peru and Chile on February 5, 2025 for 34.0 million, the Europe-North segment to Bauer Radio Limited on March 31, 2025 for 625.0 million (net cash proceeds 572.0 million, part used to prepay the 375.0 million CCIBV term loan), and Brazil on October 1, 2025 for 15.0 million (S1 page:93; S1 page:94). It used proceeds and cash on hand to reduce indebtedness by approximately 605 million in 2025 (S1 page:55). The Spain sale agreed on September 7, 2025 for approximately 115 million euros (S2 page:9; S1 page:94) completed on August 4, 2026 for a purchase price of approximately 132.3 million dollars, with net proceeds subject to adjustments and fees; the company intends to use them to reduce debt, subject to the outcome of the merger (S4 page:9; S4 page:22). That completion is a subsequent event to the June 30, 2026 balance sheet and is not in the balance-sheet figures. At the offer price, equity consideration on 509,093,845 basic shares outstanding at July 31, 2026 is about 1,237.1 million before equity awards and any other dilutive instruments (C2); the supplied sources do not state the fully diluted equity value or the enterprise value.

It combines the accepted financial base and the accepted business and transaction context, and it gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
